Amorim explains dislike for ‘AmorimBall’ term and what leaves him ‘really worried’ about Milan

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.
  • Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.

Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini. All five of their goals came via flowing counter-attacks, which has led to the tag ‘AmorimBall’ doing the rounds on social media, with many believing things are starting to truly click.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that the head coach is keeping his feet firmly on the ground though, as he spoke after the game about the need to find consistency both within matches but also from game-to-game. In this sense, Thursday’s trip to face Olympiacos is another big test.

Amorim was present in the press conference room at San Siro following the win to answer questions from journalists, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“I don’t like that expression. I think we play games to win, we want to dominate the opponent. I don’t think we succeeded today: every game has its own story, and today it was man-on-man.

“Today we didn’t have to prepare much: the idea was simply to give the ball to Pulisic, to Moreira, and then exploit the combinations of these players, the understandings they already have, and conquer space.

“Today you saw that we didn’t spend much time near the opponent’s penalty area and we scored five goals, because the space wasn’t there, it was forty meters away to attack on the run.

In a recent development, “That’s why Cisse came on to play as a striker and not, for example, Camarda: because there was space behind him and Cisse is very good at that. So, I think we’ve played very good games in the past, but today it was just a question of the quality of the players, of one-on-ones, of reading the game.

Industry observers note that “Today it wasn’t a question of the coach, I think, but of the players. And they, since it was man-on-man, just had to do what they can do. when they’re so good: beating the man and opening up space. So today the credit goes entirely to the players.”.

We’ve never seen a Rabiot like this….

In a recent development, “I watched the France game and I think he’s one of the best players on the team. So I think his importance is paramount. You can see there’s rotation, there’s a lot of talent. France has a lot of talent, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

It has been revealed that “And then, if you look at the way France play, with Mbappé, with the way all these players position themselves on the pitch, sometimes with four players with Olise as the No. 10, he has to stay there to play a different kind of game.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward, he’s the decisive element. In France, however, he has a different job to do. So it depends more on his role in the national team and his role at Milan.

According to recent reports, “This changes his way of interpreting the game, and it’s further proof of how Rabiot can play by adapting to the team he’s in. For me, therefore, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his contract renewal comes soon.”.

In a recent development, “Today’s match wasn’t just about tactics. We saw changes in position, one-on-one situations with plenty of space: it seemed like a crazy game. What I felt against Genoa and in the other matches was that we were too far away, we didn’t reach the final third of the pitch.

“We’re not like the substantial teams: if you look at the big teams, like Juventus, they might struggle to get results, but you see the volume they produce. For us, it’s a bit of the opposite, so I’m really worried that, if we don’t improve, we won’t be able to maintain this number of points.

It has been revealed that “Today, however, was a step forward: we saw many players attacking the depth, something we hadn’t seen against Ferencvaros. In the other matches, we’d managed the ball well, but today we needed pace and runs.

“We need to be able to play both games within the same game, but today was clearly the type of game we needed to win.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

Industry observers note that this was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

In a recent development, johan Manzambi heads Aston Villa in front! 🟣 https://t.co/jxZf2568Sl.

Industry observers note that it is getting hard to comprehend what Jaissle wants his team to do. The much-hyped “vertical” style looks like an ugly incarnation of the long ball football of yesteryear. They did not like it at Newcastle in the 1980s and 1990s and some fashions should never return. It is in danger of resembling a shell suit that has emerged from the back of the wardrobe for a Saturday night out.

There is so much confidence in the German in the Newcastle boardroom that they believe improvement is inevitable, but that is far from assured. Newcastle are not getting better; they are making all the same mistakes and, if anything, as an attacking force, they are looking increasingly stale and predictable. They did not have a shot on target in the first half and, other than one fantastic save in the second, Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki had nothing to do.

One of the interesting subplots to this evening’s game will be watching Johan Manzambi playing for Aston Villa.

The Switzerland international’s decision to reject Newcastle in order to sign for Villa helped convince Eddie Howe to quit in the summer.

Having already missed out on Victor Munoz, who decided to join Liverpool at the last moment, losing Manzambi - their first-choice target across the position board - was a blow Howe did not feel he could recover from.

Sources indicate that in short, he was not convinced the alternatives would give him the tools to do the job this season. Aladji Bamba, who was signed instead, has not started a game for Newcastle this season and appears to be well down the pecking order in the centre midfield under Howe’s successor Matthias Jaissle.

Manzambi had a slow start to his Villa career because of injury but he was hugely impressive at the World Cup for Switzerland and is expected to become one of the best midfield players in Europe over the next few years. Nobody can say with any degree of confidence that will be the same for Bamba.

It has been revealed that after smashing Fenerbahce on Wednesday, Unai Emery has ordered four alterations. Surprisingly, John McGinn is benched, alongside Pau Torres, Ibrahim Mbaye and Ross Barkley, who scored twice in that Champions League outing. Tyrone Mings is one of the changes and captains the visitors, while Joao Gomes, Emi Buendia and Alysson also return to the fold with Emery attempting to balance the demands of domestic and European football with a largely different squad.

By Seye Omidiora | 24 Nov 2026 14:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 14:12.

Perfect at home since the start of Conference League qualifying, Borac Banja Luka welcome Atalanta BC to Gradski Stadion Banja Luka seeking another victory in front of their supporters.

Another home triumph would lift them above Maurizio Sarri's men, who currently occupy a qualification playoff spot in the 36-club standings but harbour top-eight ambitions as the league phase enters its second half.

Vinko Marinovic's side may at the moment occupy a qualification playoff spot in 21st, but they will target further progress heading into Thursday's encounter with Atalanta.

While their only league-phase victory came between defeats to Panathinaikos and Mjallby, a return to home comforts will encourage everyone associated with Borac.

The Pride of Krajina overcame KuPS on matchday two, securing a 2-0 victory in late October to extend their perfect home record.

That sequence includes results from qualifying, when Crveno-Plavi claimed victories of 3-0, 1-0 and 3-1 over Petrocub, ML Vitebsk and Vikingur respectively.

While Atalanta should pose the greatest threat yet to Krajiski Ponos' European home winning streak, the hosts enter this week's matchday-four encounter buoyed by three consecutive victories.

The Bergamaschi may be favourites, but Sarri's men remain unconvincing despite their three-match unbeaten run.

November has certainly been eventful in Bergamo, where La Dea entered a training retreat after a humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Parma before drawing 1-1 with Kairat on matchday three to begin their current unbeaten sequence.

That draw was followed by a 1-0 victory over Monza and a thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter Milan at the weekend, when Sarri's men recovered from deficits of 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2 to snatch a point against the defending league champions.

Although they have claimed only one victory during their current unbeaten run, it represents La Dea's longest such sequence since the opening four matches of the campaign, when they recorded three wins, and they will hope to build on that progress in Banja Luka on Thursday.

Victory could lift them into the coveted top eight, although the cluster of clubs on seven points, stretching from fifth-placed Brighton & Hove Albion to 10th-placed St Truidense, means little is guaranteed for an Atalanta side currently on four as the league phase enters a crucial period.

Borac have no confirmed injury absentees, although Branimir Cipetic is expected to require an assessment before Atalanta's visit.

Luka Juricic has yet to add to his three qualifying goals, but his two league-phase assists, against Panathinaikos and KuPS, underline his broader importance to the side.

Atalanta have had four different Conference League goalscorers, with Eljif Elmas, Giacomo Raspadori, Gianluca Scamacca and Nikola Krstovic all finding the net.

Sarri has tended to rotate his squad in Europe, meaning that Charles De Ketelaere, Sunday's two-goal hero against Inter, could begin on the bench, while Lazar Samardzic, Jonathan Rowe and Kamaldeen Sulemana may all start.

La Dea have several injury concerns, with Marco Carnesecchi, Odilon Kossounou and Isak Hien all likely to miss Thursday's encounter.

Borac Banja Luka possible starting lineup:.

Jurkas; Rogan, Meijers, Sanicanin, Herera; Roguljic, Jojic, Hiros, Savic; Deket, Juricic.

Atalanta BC possible starting lineup:.

Sportiello; Bellanova, Scalvini, Obric, Bernasconi; Elmas, Pasalic; Sulemana, Samardzic, Rowe; Scamacca.

Atalanta's spirited response against Inter offered encouragement, but one victory in their last three matches hardly suggests that Sarri's men have resolved their inconsistencies.

Borac have conceded just once across four European home fixtures this season, and that defensive resilience could help them preserve their unbeaten record in Banja Luka.

Tech Report: Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.
  • Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

In a recent development, the joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

Sources indicate that she’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland.

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

In a recent development, it has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

Scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

Only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year strategy, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

They want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

Having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.

Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that in the first half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball from Cittadini, who blatantly dragged him back by the shirt. The ball rolled to Goncalo Ramos who was through on goal and had a man to his left, effectively making it a two-on-zero break with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yet, the referee Pairetto blew his whistle for a foul and highlighted a yellow card to the defender. He immediately apologised for his error in failing to play the clear advantage for the Rossoneri, in an incident reminiscent of the Junior Messias goal not given against Spezia in 2021-22.

According to recent reports, that wasn’t all, either. Nine minutes into the second half, an indirect free-kick was awarded inside the Frosinone penalty area following a clear back-pass from Calvani to Palmisani, that was actually flagged by the assistant referee and not initially given by Pairetto.

Former referee Mauro Bergonzi commented on the refereeing incidents in Milan-Frosinone to La Domenica Sportiva.

Recent findings suggest that “In the first half, the referee failed to take the lead: he missed the lead, he squandered it, if we’re being honest. The situation is this: Cittadini fouls Rabiot, who steals the ball, a clear hold, the referee hastily calls the foul, and he also realises it immediately because he stops, as if to say, ‘Wow, it’s a shame I called’ because Gonçalo Ramos was hurtling toward goal.

According to recent reports, “He apologizes, he notes: ‘No, I apologise, I’m booking the Frosinone player.’ He mentioned sorry. But this is something that really bothers you from a refereeing perspective because the lead was clear, but the referee’s gesture is commendable because he raises his hands and humbly says: ‘I made a mistake’.

“53rd minute: we rarely see them called on football pitches during matches. It’s a deliberate back pass from Calvani to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper saves it, the referee wouldn’t have called anything, he turns to the right, looks at the assistant because the assistant signals it to him.

It has been revealed that “Pairetto tells the assistant, ‘Well done’ and, to make matters worse, ‘Well done’ again. The assistant was good because he saw it perfectly correctly. He made his choice, he got it right because this is a pass, a deliberate back pass.

“Chiffi, the fourth official, is also there, pressing the button to communicate with the refereeing team via his headset, and if the assistant hadn’t seen it, the fourth official would have signaled it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

The South Shields-born player has plied his trade out east at Norwich City and Peterborough United and also way out west at Plymouth Argyle.

It's been quite a journey and now he finds himself back a fair bit closer to his native north east at Huddersfield Town, settled both on and off the pitch.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Not that his initial few months in West Yorkshire were particularly easy.

January moves are often not straightforward and so it proved for the left-sided player.

He joined a Town side wrestling with form problems - a few hours after he made his debut, Lee Grant was sacked - and the mood in the stands hardly improved as winter turned to spring.

Thankfully, the mood music is transformed these days at second-placed Town, who visit Doncaster Rovers in a Yorkshire derby on Thursday evening.

Mumba, whose partner had a baby earlier this year, said: "My family have all settled. My missus, the kids, my daughters, they're all good.

Recent findings suggest that "I've settled. This is home. Obviously, it's not far from where my actual family live, which is up north in Newcastle.

"Everything now, for me, is where I need it to be. I'm exactly where I feel like I'm meant to be at this point in my career.

According to recent reports, "I think I was closer to France when I was at Plymouth than actually to my family up north!. I've been all over the place. I started off at Sunderland and went to Norwich, Peterborough and Plymouth.

According to recent reports, "It's been quite a journey, to be fair. It's finally good to be in the middle, at the centre of everything and have the support that I have closer to me and around me.

"I also had pre-season to help me find my focus and concentration and really start again and start reaping the rewards.".

Mumba is starting to display the form which convinced Town to shelve out a significant fee of around £1million to bring him back north in the January window.

A fan favourite during his time at Home Park, Mumba played a major part in Argyle's League One title-winning campaign in 2022-23.

Highlights included a superb solo goal in the Devonians' first game back in the second-tier after a 13-year absence in August 2023 - ironically against Town.

Mumba, who signed a long-term deal with Town until at least 2029, is now chasing a second promotion from the third tier - in the blue and white of Town as opposed to the green and white of Argyle.

In a recent development, he continued: "Right now, I would say I'm getting that vibe that I got from Plymouth. For me, it's the dressing room, players and togetherness that gives you the success.

"At Norwich, it was the same. The year we got promoted at (Plymouth), I feel like that togetherness was really what was behind the success, what a lot of people don't see. Come Saturday, you're going to war with your mate.

"Whoever's next to you, you're going into the battle. You've got to have that relationship and you've got to care for each other.".

Signed on an initial loan deal until January from Championship club Lincoln City, Collins' long road back to first-team duty—after sustaining a serious knee injury at his parent club almost exactly 12 months ago—meant Rovers had to be patient regarding his availability.

The debut display of the senior striker, who turns 36 on December 1, when he came off the bench midway through the second half in Saturday's draw at Yorkshire rivals Bradford City, also preceded a bit of chatter among Rovers followers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Collins showed what he was all about, demonstrating his nous to set up Rovers' first equaliser - a brilliant overhead kick from Jordan Thomas - and leading the line in canny fashion.

Given the summer departure of Billy Sharp – a player who similarly brought leadership and nous to the table in the final third – Collins will fill a void in that regard.

The former Republic of Ireland forward has been promoted seven times in his career from the lower leagues with five different clubs – Lincoln, Derby County, Shrewsbury Town, Northampton Town and Luton Town.

There was plenty of noise in the build-up to Saturday from Collins too.

Industry observers note that rovers chief Grant McCann revealed: "We've just lacked a little bit of character at times. He's certainly not been quiet on the training ground.

According to recent reports, "You can certainly hear the noise levels lift. We did a session (on Friday) on the training pitch and had an 11 v 11 game and Collo was in the team that we were preparing against and he scored against us. And we were like: 'here we go'.

In a recent development, "I could feel the group going a wee bit quiet when we conceded the first goal (at Bradford) and Collo just picked them up and went: ''Lads. I've done this against loads of clubs, so don't be worried'.".

Another welcome returnee was experienced Matty Pearson, who cast aside a booking in the first 25 seconds to stay on message at Valley Parade in only his second league outing of the campaign following injury.

Rovers host Pearson's former club Huddersfield Town on Thursday.

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 14:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 14:11.

Getafe will be aiming to avoid a fourth straight defeat in all competitions when they continue their Conference League campaign against Saburtalo Tbilisi on Thursday night.

The visitors will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in La Liga, while Saburtalo recorded a 1-0 win over Samgurali in Georgia's top flight last time out.

Saburtalo sit 29th in the Conference League table, boasting a record of one draw and two defeats from their three matches in this season's league stage to collect one point.

The Red Eagles are the first Georgian club to compete in the Conference League league stage, and they qualified for the tournament after falling in the early rounds of both the Champions League and Europa League.

Sources indicate that levan Korgalidze's side suffered a 2-0 loss to St. Truiden in their opening match of the league stage before drawing 1-1 with Mjallby ahead of a 2-1 defeat to Copenhagen last time out.

Including qualification matches, Saburtalo have played 14 times in the Conference League, boasting a record of three wins, two draws and nine defeats.

The Red Eagles have three more games to play in the league stage of the competition, with their two matches next month against Red Star and Jablonec.

Getafe, meanwhile, were last in Conference League action on November 5, suffering a 1-0 loss to Brighton & Hove Albion.

The La Liga outfit also have a record of one draw and two defeats from their three matches in this season's league stage, which has left them down in 31st spot in the table.

Jose Bordalas' side finished seventh in last season's La Liga table, but it has been a difficult 2026-27 campaign as a whole, right now occupying 18th position in the La Liga table, while they have performed well below expectations in Europe this term.

The Deep Blue Ones have lost their last three games in all competitions, and there is pressure on them to pick up a positive result on Thursday.

Getafe's final two matches in the league stage of the Conference League will take place in December against Inter Escaldes and Ajax.

Saburtalo will be missing Giorgi Tabatadze, Andria Bartishvili and Iuri Tabatadze for their European fixture on Thursday night due to injury problems.

Amiran Dzagania has been the team's main provider of goals this season, finding the back of the net on 14 occasions in all competitions, and the 25-year-old should feature in the final third.

Meanwhile, there is also set to be a spot in the side for Jemali-Giorgi Jinjolava, who has eight goals and five assists in 30 appearances this season.

As for Getafe, Juanmi, Christantus Uche and Sebastian Boselli will miss the match due to injury problems, but Nemanja Gudelj is available after missing the Atletico game through suspension.

Djene was sent off against Atletico, but the 34-year-old is available for this match and is set to be involved against Saburtalo.

Martin Satriano, who has scored three times in 19 appearances this season, is also set to start, while there could be a position through the middle for Ivan Azon.

Makaridze; Kobuladze, Amisulashvili, Selimovic, Jinjolava; Dadiani, Kardava, Tiboue; Sikharulashvili, Dzagania, Natchkebia.

Soria; Femenia, Valou, Djene, Mojica; Gudelj, Mangala; Garcia, Satriano, Terrats; Azon.

#106519. EFL cult hero Paul Mullin on his Bradford City mistake and how Rotherham United can turn a corner

EFL cult hero Paul Mullin on his Bradford City mistake and how Rotherham United can turn a corner

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mullin joined the Bantams on loan from Wrexham in the second half of last season try to push them over the line to promotion but it did not work out as planned for him.
  • The striker started just two League One games and failed to find the net as Bradford reached the play-offs, but lost in the semi-finals to Bolton Wanderers.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mullin joined the Bantams on loan from Wrexham in the second half of last season try to push them over the line to promotion but it did not work out as planned for him.

The striker started just two League One games and failed to find the net as Bradford reached the play-offs, but lost in the semi-finals to Bolton Wanderers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His next loan, to Rotherham, has been much better for him personally, with eight goals so far, but less so the Millers, who are in the League Two relegation zone after 15 matches. Changing the second half of the equation is about cutting out the mistakes which have bedevilled the team, and 32-year-old Mullin states he has a major part to play in that.

"I'm really enjoying it," notes Mullin of his time in South Yorkshire.

Industry observers note that "I love working with the manager (Alex Bruce) and the players every single day. It's a nice place to be, but t could be a hell of a lot better. We've had so much bad luck this season.

"It's been unfortunate, as well as bad performances at times.

"Within those games we haven't won, we've probably played very, very well for 30 minutes, 40 minutes, even 60 minutes. There's been a ten-minute patch where something happened and we just couldn't seem to get the game back.

Recent findings suggest that "That's sort of been the story of our season – silly mistakes that could easily be cut out. It's things that you wouldn't expect people to make.

"Everybody has periods throughout the season where they struggle to get results.

"I know it's the start of the season, but hopefully that can be ours and it flips on its head for the rest of the season, I've got full belief we can.”.

It is perhaps no coincidence Rotherham are so error-prone when one looks at their age profile.

Sources indicate that "We've got a lot of young lads in the changing room,” he mentioned. “People don't realise when you're playing, everybody looks the same age.

"When you're young, you do make naive mistakes. You make a mistake trying to do the right thing. You're not trying to make the mistake, you're trying to do the right thing.

"As you go through men's football, you need to realise quickly there's consequences to little mistakes and they can affect the results of a game, which in turn, if they carry on, can affect the rest of a career.

"It's something you need to figure out quite quickly.

"I think we're getting better at that as time goes by and we are getting closer to where we want to be.

Industry observers note that "We're still nowhere near, but we're getting closer. Hopefully we can build on it and I've no doubt that come the end of the season, it will look a hell of a lot different.

It has been revealed that "We've probably got four players, maybe, over the age of 30 and the rest are probably under 26, so there's not really much middle ground. I suppose that's part and parcel of football.

"At Wrexham I went from middle-of-the-road to being one of the experienced ones and then Bradford was a very experienced group when I got there. It's different clubs, different scenarios and I understand why.

"As experienced players, it's up to us to try to give them as much as we can to progress and to give them the best chance of having a great career. We've got some really, really talented players and I'm looking forward to seeing how they progress.

"If we can cut out the mistakes – which aren't anything to do with tactics – and we can help each other out a little bit more in that aspect, I think we'll be fine and we will see us start to climb the table.".

A key figure and cult hero in Wrexham's rise up the division, Mullin found himself marginalised in the Championship.

He was one of three forwards signed by Bradford in January, along with Ethan Wheatley and Kayden Jackson.

It has been revealed that "Bradford was just the complete opposite of what I was told it was going to be," he said. "It's fair enough. The team was doing really well.

"I was told they were going to change to be a certain way I'd fit in.

Industry observers note that "When I got there, the manager (Graham Alexander) decided otherwise. That's his job.

"He had the team at the top end of the table, so I understand why. But equally, if it was explained that way to me before I went, then I probably wouldn't have done it.

"It was unfortunate, but it's never bothered me. It's how you're treated which is important to me and the manager was respectful about it.

"He explained that he didn't want to change any more. He basically had played that way all season, and he had a change of heart and wanted to stick with it. That's fine.".

Mullin, whose son Albi is autistic, was speaking at an event to promote the EFL's Power of 72 campaign celebrating the impact of club charities.

The striker joined an adult football session for people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), at Parkgate Astro in Rotherham.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 15:08, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 15:10.

Seeking to extend their unbeaten run through this season's Europa League, Juventus will welcome Omonia to Turin on Thursday evening.

While Juve are on track for automatic qualification to the last 16, their visitors are bound for the knockout playoffs as things stand.

More accustomed to Champions League football, Juventus have made a strong start to their campaign in Europe's second tier, claiming 10 points from a possible 12 so far.

After a 5-0 cruise at home to NEC, the Italian giants secured victory over Celta Vigo on matchday two, before playing out a 2-2 draw against Rennes.

Last time out, they retained a top-eight spot by beating AZ in Alkmaar, where Teun Koopmeiners scored against his former club in a tense 2-1 win.

Since then, results have somewhat improved in Serie A, after Juve had made an inconsistent start; four points from two games have lifted Luciano Spalletti's side up to sixth place.

Having fought back twice to salvage a draw with Fiorentina, they then put four goals past lowly Venezia, inspired by Nick Woltemade's half-time introduction from the bench.

However, Spalletti's injury-hit squad still trail 11 points behind league leaders Lazio, while Italy's tight top-four fight could go all the way.

Before facing fellow contenders Como on Sunday, Juve will aim to maintain their undefeated home record in the Europa League, having won six games and drawn nine in Turin since the competition began.

Juventus have also won all four prior meetings with Omonia Nicosia, beating them over two legs in both the 1977-78 European Cup and the 1999-00 UEFA Cup - the Cypriot side lost 10-2 on the latter occasion.

While Juve sit fifth in the Europa League table on 10 points, Omonia's tally of six leaves them 18th midway through the league phase, so defeat could see them drop into the elimination zone.

After coming through qualifying, then winning two of their first three games, Henning Berg's side suffered a 3-1 defeat to NEC on matchday four, despite seizing the lead through Lois Diony's opening goal.

Industry observers note that since that setback, they have beaten Anorthosis Famagusta and drawn 1-1 with city rivals APOEL, with Diony scoring on both occasions. As a result, the Nicosia club are fifth in the Cypriot top flight, five points shy of the summit.

Their domestic title defence may not be going to initiative, but Omonia are on track to escape a Europa League group or league phase for the first time to date - albeit potentially via the playoffs.

Juventus form (all competitions):.

Juventus still have a long absence list, and Kerim Alajbegovic is set to join it on Thursday evening, after picking up a minor thigh problem against Venezia.

Pierre Kalulu and Nico Gonzalez are expected to return from injury this weekend, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Kamil Grabara and captain Manuel Locatelli are still sidelined.

Newcastle United loanee Woltemade now has nine goal contributions for the Bianconeri, having either scored or assisted in all four Europa League appearances.

Likely to support Randal Kolo Muani up front, the German striker also ranks second for shots attempted and for open-play chances created in this season's league phase.

Meanwhile, French forward Diony should lead Omonia's attack, after scoring in three consecutive matches.

Though Hungary international Loic Nego recently returned from a layoff, Carel Eiting is still ruled out by a long-term knee injury.

Juventus possible starting lineup:.

Vicario; Celik, Gatti, Bremer, Cabal; Sarr, Koopmeiners; Conceicao, Woltemade, Boga; Kolo Muani.

Omonia possible starting lineup:.

Kaminski; Mayambela, Coulibaly, Satka, Duverne; Andreou, Maric; Ewandro, Tanase, Montnor; Diony.

Both sides have scored in every league-phase game, and the evidence suggests that trend should continue.

Juventus may be fallen giants but they are still too strong for most opponents at this level - and particularly when playing on home turf.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

As Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

Industry observers note that ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

The reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

The former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the issue – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

In a recent development, when he was taken off, Ramos highlighted a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very notable player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman said.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sources indicate that sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage mentioned when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old remarked. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

Industry observers note that “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he stated. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

Industry observers note that sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

According to recent reports, “It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really notable to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”.

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

It has been revealed that all Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

Industry observers note that with less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

According to recent reports, ‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne noted. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal.

‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

In a recent development, ‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’.

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most important thing.’.

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a upcoming contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

Industry observers note that all eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

Sources indicate that ‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most vital thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’.

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

Industry observers note that maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca said.

It has been revealed that ‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’.

But the Minsterbelles know how to handle pressure. Last season they were fighting to secure their place in Division One North for 2026/27, and they did it.

This year the ambition is greater and after three wins and a draw from nine games they sit comfortably in mid-table in the fourth tier.

Boss Hames noted: “I want to build a winning team and a winning culture and approach every game that is ahead of us correctly and professionally.”.

York also have recent cup pedigree to draw on, having reached the FA Cup fourth round for the first time in their history last season.

Industry observers note that that brings the focus to second-bottom Bradford. The sides have recent history in this division, and when they last met in the league, York won 1-0 at Horsfall Stadium.

This time the stakes are as much about the numbers in the stands as the figures on the scoreboard.

The club has been steadily pushing its home crowds up, setting a record of 291 against Wroxham in last season’s FA Cup and launching a family activity day in April.

They are set to break those attendance records this Sunday, though. For the Battle of the Cities, York made the first 500 tickets available for free, which have all now gone, with the attendance nearing 1,500. Tickets are priced adults and over-12s £5, under-11s are free. The club is urging fans to get behind the team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 24 Nov 2026 16:29, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 11:32.

Ailing giants AC Milan must try to kickstart their Europa League campaign on Thursday evening, when they visit Olympiacos at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium.

Despite their status as seven-time European champions, Milan are on course for early elimination, while their unbeaten hosts have only dropped two points so far.

Milan will head into the second half of the league phase with a point to prove, having lost three out of four games to date - including the last two without scoring.

Recently beaten by Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, Ruben Amorim's side have failed to even find the scoresheet since Goncalo Ramos struck in their lone win against Red Bull Salzburg.

A paltry tally of three points leaves the Italian heavyweights in real danger of being knocked out, as they sit 28th in the Europa League table and only the top 24 will go through.

By contrast with their continental results, Milan are showing clear signs of progress in Serie A, where they occupy fourth place, just ahead of city rivals and reigning champions Inter.

The Rossoneri have taken 15 points from the last available 18 - while scoring at least twice on each occasion - and they have only lost one domestic fixture this term.

Aiming to keep pace in the Scudetto race, Amorim's men hosted surprise high-flyers Frosinone last weekend, when they eventually cruised to a 5-1 win, with rising star Alphadjo Cisse scoring again.

However, Milan must now head to Greece, where they memorably won the 1994 Champions League final but have never beaten native hosts in six prior attempts.

In particular, Milan's two previous visits to Piraeus ended with a 2-2 draw in 1959 and a 3-1 defeat in 2018, when Olympiacos won the most recent meeting.

That was also in the Europa League, and the Greek giants at the moment sit sixth in this season's league phase - seven points clear of the Rossoneri.

As things stand, Olympiacos will directly enter the last 16, despite losing their perfect record last time out.

Across all competitions, they had won nine straight games before being held to a 0-0 draw by Rennes, which followed victories over Jagiellonia Bialystok, Marseille and Sparta Prague.

All told, Imanol Alguacil's side have lost just one of their last 18 fixtures, and Sunday's 6-2 destruction of 10-man Iraklis left them second in the Greek Super League standings.

Furthermore, Olympiacos have only suffered one defeat in their last 13 Europa League matches - while keeping nine clean sheets - so they will surely fear no-one on home turf.

Olympiacos form (all competitions):.

AC Milan form (all competitions):.

Amorim has typically shuffled his lineup for Europa League games - albeit not to positive effect - and several fringe players should feature for Milan.

Omari Hutchinson and Ardon Jashari have often played, while Cisse could start again; the new Italy international already has six Serie A goals and he scored a hat-trick away to Salzburg earlier in the campaign.

At the other end of the spectrum, experienced captain Mike Maignan can return after serving a one-match ban for his red card against Bournemouth.

Goncalo Ramos is set to overcome a minor calf problem, but the visitors must travel without Mattia Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek due to injury.

Meanwhile, Olympiacos are missing long-term absentees Ayoub El Kaabi and Yusuf Yazici, plus South American pair Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze.

Leon Bailey bagged two goals and an assist at the weekend, so he could link up with Armando Gonzalez, who is the hosts' top Europa League scorer with two.

Portuguese playmaker Jota Silva has racked up the most shots in this season's league phase; however, just two of those 17 attempts have found the target and none have hit the net.

Olympiacos possible starting lineup:.

Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

AC Milan possible starting lineup:.

Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Diawara; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Rabiot, Cisse; Ramos.

Milan may have struggled to score in Europe, but with Amorim developing an exciting front line, they average above two goals per game in Serie A and are overdue to convert some chances.

That stated, Olympiacos are a formidable force on home soil, so they can keep their unbeaten streak going with a hard-fought draw.

By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 16:33, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 16:47.

Unai Emery has made four changes to his starting lineup for Tuesday's Champions League fixture against Galatasaray.

With the condition of the RAMS Park preventing Villa from training on the surface on Monday, it felt plausible that Emery could protect some of his star players.

Instead, barring the exclusion of Pau Torres and Emiliano Buendia, the Spaniard has arguably named the strongest lineup from the options available to him.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis has moved over to right-back to replace Aaron Wan-Bissaka, with Tyrone Mings getting the nod over Torres in the middle.

Joao Gomes has returned to the midfield in place of Leon Goretzka, while John McGinn returns ahead of Buendia.

Nicolas Jackson has retained his place down the middle of the attack, with former Besiktas frontman Tammy Abraham among the substitutes.

Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho has again been left out of the Villa squad.

Meanwhile, Okan Buruk has recalled the likes of former Tottenham Hotspur defender Davinson Sanchez and ex-Wolverhampton Wanderers midfielder Mario Lemina to his Galatasaray XI.

Former Arsenal man Lucas Torreira is another ex-Premier League player to be selected in the team.

However, former Norwich City star Gabriel Sara has dropped down to the substitutes' bench, joining Leroy Sane.

Lesley Ugochukwu - on loan from Burnley - is also kept in reserve, but top goalscorer Victor Osimhen remains sidelined through injury.

Galatasaray XI: Ugurcan; Singo, Sanchez, Bardakci, Jakobs; Torreira, Lemina, Elmali; Akgun, Batrakov, Yilmaz.

Subs: Bitshiabu, Sara, Gul, Gundogan, Guvenc, Lus, Nhaga, Sane, Ugochukwu, Yilmaz.

Aston Villa XI: Suzuki; Harwood-Bellis, Lindelof, Mings, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson.

Subs: Bizot, Wright, Barkley, Buendia, Torres, Abraham, Mbaye, Bogarde, Goretzka, Wan-Bissaka, Hemmings.

Bradford City 3 Barnsley FC 0: Rinse and repeat for rock-bottom Reds as visiting fans vent their ire at end

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is one etched into Barnsley folklore.
  • At the minute, Barnsley supporters have only memories to cling onto.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is one etched into Barnsley folklore. Bradford City were famously the opposition as the Reds provided one of those wonderful, soul-enhancing moments that lights up football from time to time as they reached the top-flight for the first occasion in their history.

At the minute, Barnsley supporters have only memories to cling onto. It’s pretty grim in the present - with just over a month to go, 2026 has already marked itself out as one of the most inauspicious in the Reds’ modern-day history.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

According to recent reports, how they needed something on a cold, dank West Yorkshire night. Ten without a league win in an appalling autumn, two points from a possible 30, propping up the table and with growing fears that they could drop into the fourth tier for the first time since 1978-79 if the narrative doesn’t change.r.

City, for their part, were in no mood to be charitable and sympathetic after tough derby moments against Doncaster Rovers and Huddersfield Town in their previous two league matches, both at Valley Parade.

Despite missing chances to make the night more straightforward after an early opener, they eventually found a way midway through the second half.

To rub salt into Reds’ wounds, it was former Oakwlel striker Stephen Humphrys who did the damage with his second of the night as he scored for the third successive game as City ended the glut of home games in the right fashion from their perspective.

A third in stoppage time from the spot, from Jake Beesley, was the prelude to chants of ‘You’re not fit to wear the shirt’ from disgruntled Reds followers.

The pre-match portents weren’t great for the Reds. Reyes Cleary, who scored one of the EFL’s goals of the season from some 70 yards here last autumn, was absent through illness.

Cam McGeehan did at least return from suspension - as did ex-City loanee Jack Shepherd - while there was a rare start for Tyrese Noslin.

The hosts made four changes, including a first in their three-man backline since September 1.

Macaulay Gillesphey got the nod, on his 31st birthday, with ex-Reds duo Adam Phillips and Humphrys also starting alongside Will Swan - the front three who finished the weekend derby against Doncaster Rovers.

Beesley was back on the bench for the hosts after recovering from a knock.

It was a bit of a Groundhog Day half from Barnsley, truth be told.

Again, they revealed evidence that between both boxes, there are certainly far worse teams at this level. In their defensive duties, there are surely no-one worse and as Daniel Stendel remarked beforehand, getting it right in both boxes wins and loses football matches.

City led 1-0 at the interval and given events on Saturday, when they failed to get a two-goal cushion against another struggling White Rose visitor, there should have been understandable disappointment.

Humphrys ‘old-manned’ Barnsley’s meek and ineffectual backline and was too much for them in the first half. He could easily have laid claim to the matchball.

His opener was helped by some pitiful defending.

Direct from a goalkick, Jon McCracken revealed quick thinking like on Saturday. Humphrys brushed aside the meek Sam Gale far too easily and the covering from Arley Kay was similarly powder-puff and he easily converted as the Reds conceded early for the second successive derby.

Gale and Kay would later switch positions as Barnsley morphed into a back three.

Bradford were only too happy to stick it on Barnsley’s flaky defence and go direct and there were gaping holes to exploit on occasions.

Humphrys soon played in Kayden Jackson, in oceans of space, but Cieran Slicker saved at his near post.

Humphrys also found a hole to exploit in the box and headed over from Ibou Touray’s cross, while Swan also fired a good chance wide after being sent clear by Callum Connolly’s pass. Later on in the half, Phillips headed a decent opportunity off target.

At the other end, Barnsley’s best chance came in the first few minutes when Patrick Kelly cashed in on Matt Pennington’s loose clearance, but McCracken parried his well-struck half-volley - straight at him instead of a yard either side.

McGeehan also blasted a presentable chance over. In both boxes, it was as you were for the ailing Reds.

On the restart, Barnsley were afforded a sniff with his crisp low shot from Ryan Brownlie’s low shot flashing just wide following Ziyad Larkeche’s cross before a skewed high clearance from Connolly had to be tipped over in the nick of time by McCracken.

Despite their side’s form, the backing from the stoic band of visiting supporters was impressive.

Those in visiting jerseys, for all their deficiencies in defence, had a good dig at the start of the second period.

City gradually awoke and Connolly fired a loose ball wide following consternation in the Reds box. At the other end, Kelly lashed a shot into the empty Bradford end before Connell fired straight at McCracken.

Substitute Makenzie Kirk was then off beam, with home punters starting to get a touch agitated at the lack of a second goal at the other end.

They were soon appeased when astute hold-up play from Powell teed up Humphrys, who rammed home a second.

McCracken then grasped a free-kick from Connell, one of the few visiting players who managed to convince.

Winter is nigh and it looks like being a long and hard one for Barnsley unless they get January right.

Beesley added a third in stoppage time from the spot.

Recent findings suggest that bradford City: McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Gillesphey (Pratt 82); Jackson, Connolly, Morgan, Touray; Phillips (Neufville 57), Swan (Powell 57); Humphrys (Beesley 74). Substitutes unused: Hadi, Matthews, O’Keeffe.

It has been revealed that barnsley: McCracken; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche (Johnson 78); Connell, McGeehan; Noslin (Reid 84), Kelly, Brownlie (Kirk 63); Yoganathan. Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, O’Riordan, Okedina, Alker.

If only they had played the first half as they had the second, perhaps they might have been celebrating victory rather than a point which felt like one, thanks to the timing of Peck's goal.

If the first half demonstrated how short the Blades are of the very best in the division, the second showed what they have in their locker to try to do something about it.

Southampton will have walked off more relieved to take the point than the home team.

The Saints took the lead in the 11th minute when Hamza Choudhury gave the ball away and was unable to close Lewis Dobbin down before he curled a beautiful shot inside the far post.

Already by then it was on the cards, with Saints dominating possession as James Ward-Prowse pulled the strings in midfield.

The only saving grace is that the Blades only trailed 1-0 at the break.

Mads Roerslev had a shot blocked and Kuryu Matsuki thrashed an effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

The Blades did at least improve as half-time approached, Mark McGuinness heading a Peck corner, and Romelle Donovan - switched to the right - came inside and shot at the goalkeeper.

With Patrick Bamford introduced at the break, the Blades were much sharper in the second half.

Peck's shot from distance in the 50th minute demonstrated ambition, if not accuracy.

Industry observers note that A couple of minutes later, Bamford headed over at a corner nodded to him by Mark McGuinness. Next was Ayew, who headed at Daniel Peterz after Donovan got to the byline to tee the chance up.

Ayew was released down the left but delayed too long, and could only force a corner from a tight angle.

Donovan had a penalty appeal waved away, perhaps not helped by the fact he was clearly looking for it.

But the football was as one-way as the first half had been, only with more chances to show from it.

Chong was unable to keep his shot down when the ball dropped to him 16 yards out, and Harrison Burrows had an effort blocked.

Southampton briefly provided some variety in the 80th minute when Donovan blocked Cyle Larin and Ward-Prowse ballooned the follow-up over, but the play quickly moved back to the Kop End.

Chong's cross went all the way through to Burrows at the back post, but he could only loop his header up for Peretz to catch.

But the gilt-edged chance fell to Chong in the 83rd after a lovely move through Ayes and Bamford. The winger steered his shot into the right place, but Peretz stretched out brilliantly to his right to save it.

When that was squandered, it felt like the Blades might run out of time.

But in the 90th minute Ayew did brilliantly to dribble along the byline and pull the ball back for Peck to find the net through a busy penalty area.

It could have counted for nought had Cooper not intervened in the 95th minute.

As saves go, it was a pretty significant one.

Sheffield United: Cooper; Choudhury (McCallum 87), McGuinness, Kitching, Burrows; Chong (Campbell 87), Peck, Arblaster (Phillips 69), Donovan; Cannon (Bamford HT), Ayew (Sidibe 90+3).

Unused substitutes: Davies, Norrington-Davies, Baptiste, Riedewald.

Southampton: Peretz; Roerslev (Bree 59), Abbott, Wood, Welington; Bragg (Azaz 59); Downes, Ward-Prowse; Matsuki (Stephens 87), Mubama (Larin 59), Dobbin (Edozie 70).

Unused substitutes: Manning, Fellows, Long, Williams.

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has become the latest ex-Red Devil to tear into the club's defence, criticising Leny Yoro following his red card in his side's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's clash with their rivals at Anfield on Sunday, tripping Alexander Isak as he ran in on goal after an error from Matthijs de Ligt.

He has had a mixed time of things since his £52million move to Old Trafford in 2024, though has been playing in a leaky United defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches this season – with only Crystal Palace conceding more.

Several different members of United's defence have come under fire this season, and, on Monday, it was the turn of Yoro.

'The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him,' Scholes noted on The Good, The Bad and The Football, sponsored by Midnite.

He added: 'You know what, he’s come in to a really bad setup defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to (Virgil) Van Dijk he might look a little bit better but he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights.'.

Paul Scholes (pictured) has suggested Leny Yoro is not yet ready for the Premier League.

Yoro was sent off in the opening minutes of Manchester United's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that fellow former United midfielder Nicky Butt, who played alongside Scholes for United between 1994 and 2004, added: 'If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea. He’s a great talent that will come good.'.

Scholes, though, wasn't having any of it.

He replied: 'I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is. I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races. Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, oh, what do I do?'.

United have also faced criticism for their apparent lack of running this season, with eyebrows raised when Youri Tielemans said in the summer that they didn't do much prior to the campaign getting under way.

Sources indicate that the club rank 17th for distance covered in the top flight this season, with Liverpool, Brentford and Everton below them. The latter two will almost certainly pass them though after their game on Monday.

That, according to Butt, is down to the players.

According to recent reports, 'We’ve had our say about the players and they’re just not good enough,' he said. 'It is the most unathletic team I’ve ever seen in Man United.

'I’m going to go through a team and I’m trying to be as honest as I can. Forget the quality for right now. For me, physicality-wise, if you go through a team, the right back, he’s physically OK, but he’s not amazing. De Ligt or Harry, whoever he’s going to play in there, physically not great. Martinez for me is physically not great. You got Yoro who will physically come good.

Nicky Butt (pictured), meanwhile, has criticised the physical ability of many of United's players.

Industry observers note that 'Then I go on to the midfield, none of them are physically good enough. Kobbie can get about the pitch 15-20 yards, but he’s not box to box. Said that numerous times. He’s got a lot of talent. He’s got a lot of things going for him. I think he’s a top player. He ain’t got the legs. He needs to have legs around him but his legs around him at the minute are Bruno and Tielemans - and they can’t run around.

In a recent development, 'Look at Mbeumo, I think he’s OK but he’s not going to blow anybody away. I think Cunha can run. So then you look at the whole squad and you’re saying three players can run.

'What I’m getting at there, and it sounds like I’m being a draconian but what you have to do first and foremost when you go to Anfield is to be able to compete physically and they can’t so they have no chance.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

Sources indicate that earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology firm called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary latest proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary new proteins.

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

Sources indicate that and on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed fresh proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

Recent findings suggest that the research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” indicates Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

Industry observers note that but some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

The release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 launched a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing newly introduced proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, indicates Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

To see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

Recent findings suggest that in other experiments, the OpenAI team highlighted that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

In a recent development, jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, believes that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in even each capability,” he indicates.
