This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC.

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

It has been revealed that eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

“We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta mentioned. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

Recent findings suggest that “The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

Recent findings suggest that “I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”.

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO.

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a massive moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”.

Sources indicate that forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Murillo had Forest’s best opportunity two minutes into injury time after cutting inside the penalty area but could not find the top corner.

Another defeat will only add to their concerns and Glasner needs to quickly find a solution or face another relegation battle.

It does not promise to get easier immediately, either, with Manchester City, Chelsea and Brighton up next in the league at home, but there were encouraging signs here, despite the club sitting in the bottom three.

Glasner stated: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

It has been revealed that “It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”.

We knew the margins would be really small. They are extremely well coached and organised. The longer the game goes on they gain more belief. But we have players with different qualities and can adapt to what the game is delivering.

We have another three substantial chances that should be goals. That is the difference, you have to be clinical. If we keep generating them, they will come.

Recent findings suggest that let’s enjoy the win, because it was a very tough one. And then, on Wednesday, we have an incredible game against Bayern Munich away [in the Champions League].

Recent findings suggest that when you see their goal it’s deflected otherwise, it’s straight to the gloves of Matz Sels. You have periods in football where you feel everything going against you and then there are periods when things are on your side.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

And having this coolness, not to worry too much because I can see good performances and not good results. The results will come if the performances stay good.

Noni [Madueke], Jurrien [Timber], Mikel [Merino] was brilliant when he came on and Viktor [Gyokeres] really changed the game - all of them did and that’s what we need. Noni obviously the highlight because he scored the goal and that’s the difference.

Sometimes you can get frustrated with teams who are difficult to break down. First half we didn’t have a shot on target and that’s something we discussed. We had another two significant ones in the second half but the only one on target we had was a little deflection and it’s in.

Great reaction [after scoring goal], to have the will to defend a really open and difficult and stressful situation.

We knew it would be a tough game, it always is against Arsenal. They have a good team. But we feel we can change the result, maybe a draw, maybe a win. Now we have to put it in the past and focus on the next match.

If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd so we know that we’re going to start some and finish some and for me it’s the same mentality every time I just want to create or score.

Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.

Recent findings suggest that we have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. Great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.

  • Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.
  • Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

It’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s new financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

United also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January.

Pochettino is only expected to make two latest signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre).

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

Gyokeres nets stunner as Arsenal held by Dortmund in thriller.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Latest score and updates Champions League.

Man Utd make Pro Ref decision amid Pochettino red card rage.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

Industry observers note that it was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

It has been revealed that that happened against Slavia Prague, when the Gunners just about held on in the second half to win. It happened on Saturday, when they had to come from behind just to draw a match they should have been three or four goals up in.

And it happened here, in perhaps the most ridiculous way yet. With some better decision-making in the final third, the Premier League champions might have put six past Dortmund.

Recent findings suggest that instead, from their 30 shots, Arsenal managed just four shots on target and one goal. The visitors rode their luck but they stayed within touch and when their moment came, Maximilian Beier took it with the kind of ruthlessness Arteta can only dream of.

It is unrealistic to expect the north Londoners to dominate a match for the full 90 minutes, even more so against Dortmund than the likes of Slavia Prague and Newcastle.

The problem is Arsenal’s lack of efficiency when they are on top means they cannot afford even the slightest drop in standards or intensity.

Score the two or three goals that the dominance deserves in the first half and a dip after the break will not be so decisive. As it is, with Arsenal leaving the margins so thin, one moment is all it takes for the hard work to be undone.

Recent findings suggest that at St James’ Park, that moment was Odegaard mis-kicking a clearance. Here, it was Joane Gadou charging away from Christos Tzolis and nobody in the home midfield coming across to cover.

The match should have been done by then. Again, Arsenal were sensational in the first 45 minutes.

It has been revealed that noni Madueke, a constant threat, could not sort his feet out quickly enough when a rebound fell to him. The winger was then completely open, screaming for the ball shortly after when Declan Rice instead went by himself and had his shot deflected wide.

Counters were wasted. Viktor Gyokeres, who opened the scoring with a superb strike from distance, suddenly could not hit the target. When Arsenal went in only 1-0 up, what followed next was as predictable as it was galling for the Gunners.

The level dropped just slightly and the Bundesliga leaders came back into the game, equalising ten minutes after the restart.

Even then, though, Arsenal should have been able to recover. Unlike against Slavia Prague or Newcastle, Arsenal did not fall away for an extended period. This match was there for them to win and the chances came thick and fast.

Gyokeres headed wide from a few yards out. The Arsenal fans spent almost the entire final half an hour screaming at the players to shoot as extra touches were taken around the area.

When Serhou Guirassy then bounced the ball off his body onto his own post not once but twice, Arteta collapsed to the ground in disbelief.

Recent findings suggest that the winner would not come. A top-two finish, which was so key in last season’s run to the final, has now become much harder.

In a recent development, but that is what this side keep doing. They seem determined to make things hard for himself. Another match that should have been won inside an hour turned into a 90-minute slugfest.

With Arsenal hoping this is another long season domestically and in Europe, it is a habit they must shake fast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 17:13.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has dropped a worrying admission over Ryan Gravenberch's fitness ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge.

The Dutchman has missed each of the Reds' last three games with a heel fracture and was unsurprisingly not included in Liverpool's 22-man squad for the trip to the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Gravenberch had returned to training before Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League affair, but the former Ajax man is still no closer to a competitive comeback.

After landing in Belgium, Iraola fielded questions from the media in his pre-game press conference, and he admitted that Gravenberch's injury was proving more complex to solve than initially anticipated.

In a recent development, "With Ryan, it's a bit more difficult," Iraola mentioned. "He's having pain, the things in the fascia are difficult to solve. Sometimes he's managing the pain, but now he's not in a good place. Let's see if we can find ways to solve the problem but they are injuries that are not easy to solve normally.".

While the exact nature and severity of Gravenberch's injury is not entirely clear, the Netherlands international may be suffering from Plantar fasciitis, which would fit Iraola's description.

An inflammation of the heel, Plantar fasciitis can take anywhere between four and 12 weeks to get better, and Gravenberch has already been out since the beginning of November.

As a result, the Dutchman may be missing until the end of January in the worst-case scenario, meaning he would firstly miss matches against Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Porto and Aston Villa before the end of the year.

Liverpool then face Manchester United, Inter Milan and Everton again in the early weeks of 2027, and it remains to be seen if Gravenberch's complex matter has settled down by then.

The 24-year-old has set up one goal in 12 appearances for Liverpool so far this season, and in his absence, Alexis Mac Allister, Trey Nyoni, Dominik Szoboszlai and James McConnell will be competing for midfield minutes.

As well as delivering a negative patch on Gravenberch, Iraola also revealed that Cody Gakpo would likely miss the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton too.

The attacker hurt his calf while representing the Netherlands during the international break, although Iraola has insisted that his matter is not severe.

"With Cody, it's a soleus injury," Iraola added. "It's not big but we expect he'll be out for the weekend. But it's more predictable.".

Giovanni Leoni (knee), Conor Bradley (knee) and Hugo Ekitike (Achilles) are also on the sidelines for Liverpool, who sit eighth in the Champions League league-phase table with nine points from their opening four fixtures.

Mauricio Pochettino’s priority in the January transfer window will not centre on strengthening Manchester United’s leaky defence.

After Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing at the hands of Liverpool, the Red Devils now possess the most porous rearguard in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor was given an instant reality check at Anfield and is now fully aware of the size of the task he faces with United entrenched in the relegation zone after 11 matches.

Pochettino attempted to shake things up defensively yesterday with Matthijs de Ligt handed a surprise start, but the Netherlands international, still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was given the run around by Liverpool’s spritely attack.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, was sent-off after just eight minutes and the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot also hardly covered themselves in glory in the face of relentless pressure from Andoni Iraola’s side.

Despite the obvious defensive complications, the other end of the pitch represents equal concern for Pochettino.

United opted against signing a newly introduced forward in the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired given the setbacks encountered by Benjamin Sesko.

The Slovenia international displayed signs of promise after a difficult start to his United career last season following his £74million move from RB Leipzig.

A nagging shin injury has restricted the 23-year-old to just six appearances so far this term and he is unlikely to return until the Newly introduced Year at the earliest.

As a result, United have been forced to alternate between Bryan Mbuemo and Matheus Cunha in central striking roles with Joshua Zirkzee largely untrusted.

United’s brains trust has just over a month to consider their options when it comes to recruiting a latest forward.

Folarin Balogun, the Monaco striker, wants to be reunited with Pochettino, who coached the former Arsenal player during his tenure as USA head coach.

‘I’m sure in the upcoming transfer windows, I’ll look to leave again,’ Balogun, who almost joined Everton last summer, said.

‘I think my point of view was very clear.’.

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering newly introduced insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, indicates Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

According to recent reports, PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

The study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Sources indicate that many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” says study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

Sources indicate that the study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

The researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

Industry observers note that the amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

Jobe Bellingham has revealed an Arsenal weakness that he and Borussia Dortmund looked to exploit in their Champions League encounter.

The Bundesliga leaders left the Emirates Stadium with a share of the spoils after Maximilian Beier’s equaliser cancelled out Viktor Gyokeres’ stunning opener in the first half.

The Gunners had plenty of chances to kill the game off and secure all three points, but Declan Rice hit the post, Noni Madueke went close a number of times and Gyokeres missed a gilt-edged opportunity from close range as they were forced to settle for a stalemate.

Post-match, Bellingham, fresh off his maiden senior England call-up, said that there had been a “mismatch” that he was instructed to take advantage of in midfield.

“One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly],” he explained on Amazon Prime Video.

“For the long ball - I don’t want to say a mismatch - but I’m obviously bigger.

In a recent development, “You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls. I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch.

“We varied it well, we played short, and we retained possession and defended a lot better in transitions.”.

Jobe, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude, was unfortunate not to hit the winner as he followed in Julian Ryerson’s saved shot, which Kepa Arrizabalaga spilled.

Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins has been touted as a target, but the 25-year-old would not be a cheap option.

The Bees paid £23m for him when they signed him from Wolves three years ago and he remains under contract until 2029.

Arsenal were fortunate not to concede a penalty against Borussia Dortmund during their Champions League draw.

The Premier League champions and Bundesliga leaders held each other to a 1-1 stalemate at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres’ rifled opener was cancelled out in the second half by Maximilian Beier.

It was the Gunners’ second draw on the spin after a 2-2 encounter at St James’ Park, where Noni Madueke rescued a point against Newcastle after Malick Thiaw and Harvey Barnes had put the Magpies ahead following Eberechi Eze’s opening goal.

But it was the goalscorer Gyokeres who almost turned from hero to villain, as he allegedly handled a Dortmund corner in the second period.

It led Amazon Prime Video pundits Alan Shearer and Mark Clattenberg to question referee Maurizio Mariani’s decision not to award a spot kick to the visitors.

“I think Arsenal were fortunate to have gotten away with that one,” Shearer remarked on co-commentary.

"I know it might have been Fabio Silva in front of him trying to flick it on, but he didn't, and his arm is actually out.".

Clattenberg, said alongside the record Premier League goalscorer in the north London gantry, concurred.

"We all know UEFA have a stricter handball rule than we see in the Premier League, but what doesn't save Gyokeres in this situation is, the ball comes in from a distance and he makes a little movement of his arm towards the ball so that makes it look more like a penalty kick for me,” the former official mentioned.

Former Arsenal forward Theo Walcott spoke of his relief at the penalty not being given.

"As soon as it hit his hand, straight away my heart is in my mouth, I think it's a penalty," he said.

In a recent development, "I think he's got away with that. I'm pleased it wasn't given because it's not a penalty, but in Europe it probably should be.".

Gyokeres asserted his innocence in his post-match interview.

"I think the arm was towards my body," the Swede said.

"I don't think it was outside, so I don't think it was anything.".

The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was unveiled to much fanfare on Monday.
  • Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026.

The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was unveiled to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian mentioned, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England.

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

Recent findings suggest that what the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed latest 100,000 stadium.

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed upcoming 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

Industry observers note that it cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole stated of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve said it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

It has been revealed that ‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

Sources indicate that ‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

After making his debut in 2003, Ronaldo led Portugal to their first-ever major trophy at Euro 2016 and also won the Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

His time with Portugal ended abruptly, with the 41-year-old leaving their camp midway through the September-October international break after a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.

He was subsequently given a 30-day suspension by the FPF, though he announced his retirement ahead of the November break.

The FPF noted they would initiative a farewell for Ronaldo, and Guardiola has urged them to do so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are noted to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

Recent findings suggest that ‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

It has been revealed that varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

Industry observers note that ‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

  • Manchester United have been boosted by the return of Luke Shaw for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Portuguese giants Sporting Lisbon.
  • Shaw has not featured for Man United since October 10 due to a muscular problem, but he returned to training ahead of the European match and has been named in the travelling squad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 18:29.

Manchester United have been boosted by the return of Luke Shaw for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Portuguese giants Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has not featured for Man United since October 10 due to a muscular problem, but he returned to training ahead of the European match and has been named in the travelling squad.

The Englishman's return is major news for the Red Devils given their defensive problems, but it remains to be seen whether he is considered for a start on Wednesday.

Matheus Cunha is a notable absentee through suspension, with the Brazil international sent off in the team's last match in the competition against Roma.

Meanwhile, Carlos Baleba, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain sidelined alongside long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte.

Man United have six points to show from their four matches in the competition, which has left them in 18th in the overall table.

Head coach Mauricio Pochettino has major decisions to make when it comes to his defensive unit for this match, as Matthijs de Ligt struggled in the 4-0 loss to Liverpool last time out.

Leny Yoro had been facing a Premier League suspension, increasing his chances of being involved from the first whistle against Sporting.

However, Yoro's red card against Liverpool has been overturned following a successful appeal.

The 21-year-old will therefore now be available to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Karl Darlow has also returned to the squad for the Sporting trip, having recovered from the injury that forced him to miss out against Liverpool.

Goalkeepers: Senne Lammens, Karl Darlow, Tom Heaton.

Defenders: Harry Amass, Diogo Dalot, Matthijs de Ligt, Patrick Dorgu, Ayden Heaven, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, Noussair Mazraoui, Luke Shaw, Leny Yoro.

Midfielders: Andrey Santos, Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Mason Mount, Youri Tielemans.

Forwards: Amad, Shea Lacey, Bryan Mbeumo, Joshua Zirkzee.

Manchester United have added another experienced Premier League centre-half to their list of targets ahead of the transfer window opening.

After leaking four goals in another humbling defeat at Anfield on Sunday, Mauricio Pochettino has inherited the worst defence in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor is said to be keen on adding a striker to his ranks to cover for the injured Benjamin Sesko, but tightening up his backline will also represent a priority.

Fulham’s Calvin Bassey emerged as a potential target last week, but the versatile defender is reported to be close to signing a contract extension with the London club.

According to talkSPORT, United have also identified Brentford’s Nathan Collins as a possible solution to a problem that has plagued successive managers.

The Red Devils also have maintained an interest in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite but he is likely to prove too expensive, given they are reported to have a budget of just £50million to work with.

Collins, 25, is under contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029 and would also command a significant fee.

While reinforcements would certainly aid United’s cause, former club captains Roy Keane and Gary Neville fear it is not just defenders their old side are in need of.

‘My worry for United’s defenders [is] they’re not getting great help,” remarked Keane after the Anfield drubbing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

According to recent reports, this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

According to recent reports, ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

Iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola said. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha said to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

Iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

Recent findings suggest that iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola remarked of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he stated, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

Defending champions Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the table to six points after a hard-fought draw away at Newcastle.

Brighton had the chance to cut that lead to just three points, but a late Oli McBurnie brace saw them lose 2-0 to Hull City on Sunday.

Manchester City did snap their three-match losing streak, but a 1-1 draw on Fulham means Enzo Maresca’s side are now winless in four Premier League matches and also six points off the league leaders.

City will have the opportunity to eat into Arsenal’s lead at the top of the table when the two sides meet at the Emirates next week.

However, Butt does not expect them to last the course in this season’s title race, instead talking up Liverpool’s chances after their impressive 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday.

‘Any win for Liverpool against Man United or vice versa is massive,’ Butt noted on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

‘Forget the ten men or the level of the team they are playing against at the time. When Liverpool beat Man United or the other way around, it’s a massive result, especially for a fresh manager.

‘It was only a couple of years ago that they won the league, so they’re not a bad team, and they’ve added well.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Mikel Arteta provided a coy enhancement on David Raya’s availability for Arsenal’s showdown with Manchester City this weekend.

The goalkeeper missed the Gunners’ draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night with a shoulder injury that he picked up against Newcastle.

The Spaniard left the pitch at St James’ Park in significant pain and Arsenal feared a lengthy absence, but scans proved to be positive.

The No1 has avoided a serious injury and he will not require surgery, though there is uncertainty over exactly when he will return.

There are suggestions that the goalkeeper will only be out for a matter of days and could be in contention to face City on Sunday.

However, Arteta refused to confirm that.

“No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately,” Arteta remarked after his side’s 1-1 draw with Dortmund.

“We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].”.

In Raya’s absence, Kepa Arrizabalaga started against Dortmund, as Arsenal had to settle for just a point despite a dominant performance.

The Spaniard was fairly comfortable throughout, though he did have some shaky moments from corners and when rolling the ball out to Myles Lewis-Skelly to play him into trouble.

However, it was an improvement on Kepa’s display in the Carabao Cup final last season and solid enough to be confident he will keep his place over Illan Meslier while Raya remains out.

Kepa has had limited football since joining the club, so trusted has Raya become for Arsenal, but Arteta insisted he will have full faith in the goalkeeper if he is required to start in goal against City.

“Him and Illan, they’re both in the same situation,” Arteta said.

“I think Kepa had a really good performance today. We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.”.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:56 EST, 23 November 2026.

Jack Grealish returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being made unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline, and came off the bench at half-time against Brentford on Monday.

In a recent development, the Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He had not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a 'breach of club discipline' and a lack of fitness thereafter.

He last featured on October 17, over a month ago, but returned to the match day squad to take on Brentford on Monday night – named on the substitutes' bench. He was introduced at half-time for Tyrique George, with the Toffees 2-0 down and down to 10 men after James Tarkowski's red card. They would ultimately lose 4-0.

Manager David Moyes said ahead of the game: 'He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

Sources indicate that 'We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don't want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn't be.'.

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: 'He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?'.

Jack Grealish (right) returned to Everton action on Monday for the first time since being punished for missing training.

He was named on the bench against Brentford, coming on for Tyrique George at half-time.

Industry observers note that everton had won their last three games and went into Monday's match sixth in the table. The result, though, was a blow as they dropped to ninth.

Asked what Grealish can offer, Moyes added: 'Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

According to recent reports, 'But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

'I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.'.

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

According to recent reports, 'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart emoji)'.

  • In a recent development, while Senegal won 1-0 against Morocco in the final of AFCON 2025, the match was beset by controversy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Moroccan FA say they initiative to explore all legal avenues to appeal after expressing their “protest” against the CAS ruling to reinstate Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners.

In a recent development, while Senegal won 1-0 against Morocco in the final of AFCON 2025, the match was beset by controversy. Senegal players and staff left the pitch in the 98th minute in protest against the award of a penalty for the hosts, which left the game paused for 14 minutes. The match eventually resumed, Brahim Diaz missed the spot kick and the game went to extra time, which saw Senegal score and go on to lift the trophy.

But African football governing body CAF retrospectively awarded the title to Morocco two months after the final, stating that Senegal’s conduct during the match had disqualified them as winners. Morocco were named automatic 3-0 winners.

The Senegalese FA took an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) which, after a months-long saga, reinstated Senegal as champions on Tuesday.

But Morocco have not given up, citing reports of an alleged telephone conversation between CAS panelist Ulrich Haas and the president of Senegal’s football federation hours before Tuesday’s ruling as one reason they have grounds for an appeal.

Recent findings suggest that the CAS ruling noted: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).

“By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

In a recent development, “In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

“Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.”.

Senegal awarded Afcon 2025 title by CAS verdict as Morocco stripped.

But Morocco have vowed to appeal CAS’s ruling.

A statement from the Moroccan FA stated: “We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.”.

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for Saturday's Premier League clash against Brentford, with his one-game suspension being removed.

Yoro was sent off in the early stages of Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool following a last-man challenge on Reds forward Alexander Isak.

The France international was facing a one-game suspension, ruling him out of Man United's next Premier League fixture against Brentford.

However, the ban has now been removed following a successful appeal.

"Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," read a statement from the Football Association.

Recent findings suggest that "The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course.".

There had been a lot of debate surrounding whether the foul was a clear denial of a goalscoring opportunity, as Isak appeared to lose possession of the ball.

Industry observers note that breaking: Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool has been overturned.? https://t.co/GIdwIWXdUs.

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo both criticised the decision in their post-match comments.

According to recent reports, "The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak," mentioned Pochettino.

"When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper.".

Mainoo, meanwhile, said: "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card. No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper.".

Yoro is currently with the Man United squad in Portugal preparing for Wednesday's Champions League fixture with Sporting Lisbon.

During his two seasons at United, Hojlund scored 26 goals in 95 appearances.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Edward Iordanescu has been appointed as Watford's new head coach, three days after Alessio Dionisi was sacked.

Dionisi was only in charge for five months, with his sacking coming on the back of a run of seven defeats in 10 league games, culminating in a 4-0 loss to Sheffield United.

That result left Watford 20th in the Championship table, three points above the relegation zone, with Iordanescu becoming their sixth new boss in less than 18 months.

He is also the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

"I am very proud and happy to be at this football club," Iordanescu told the club website.

"I can see the team is in a difficult moment, but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days, and I'm very confident about the future.

According to recent reports, "I will put all my passion into my job, and I will demand the full commitment of everybody. It all starts with hard work – the rest will follow.

"I look forward to meeting the fans at the game [on Wednesday] and starting work.".

Industry observers note that edward Iordănescu is our fresh Head Coach. Welcome, Edward. https://t.co/E0wum5RdDR https://t.co/6aC3X7Kd54.

— Watford Football Club (@WatfordFC) November 25, 2026.

Iordanescu's first game in charge of Watford will come against Derby County on Saturday, but he will be in the stands for Wednesday's clash with Blackburn Rovers.

This will be the 48-year-old's first job since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, having led the side to the Polish Super Cup in July 2025.

Iordanescu also took charge of Romania for two and a half years, guiding them to the last 16 at Euro 2024 when they were beaten by the Netherlands.

Unai Emery delivered a blunt assessment of Alejandro Garnacho’s situation at Aston Villa after the Argentine was left out of the squad for the defeat to Galatasaray on Tuesday night.

Villa were beaten 1-0 in Turkey and now sit ninth in the Champions League table, one place outside the automatic qualification spots.

Garnacho, meanwhile, trained with his Villa teammates on Monday but he was not even named on the bench against Galatasaray.

The on-loan Chelsea winger was also not included in Villa’s squad for their goalless draw at home to Sunderland on Saturday.

For the game against Galatasaray, Emery only picked 11 substitutes out of a possible 12 and also included two goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s absence after Villa’s defeat, Emery replied: ‘Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us, to play with us.’.

Garnacho has made just seven appearances since joining Villa in the summer and is yet to score a goal or register an assist.

Villa have an obligation to buy Garnacho from Chelsea for £43 million but only if he makes a certain number of appearances this season.

Chelsea signed Garnacho in a £40m deal from Manchester United last year but the Argentine struggled to make an impact during his time at Stamford Bridge, scoring eight goals in 43 appearances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

According to recent reports, the own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, in the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

It has been revealed that I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the newly introduced coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

Sources indicate that the vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a major gap in that midfield.

In a recent development, to continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Sources indicate that yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

It has been revealed that on top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

Industry observers note that it was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

Sources indicate that I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

In a recent development, truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

In a recent development, amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around promptly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be mentioned that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 18:54, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 19:11.

Enzo Maresca has made a total of five changes to his Manchester City starting lineup for tonight’s Champions League clash against Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

Matheus Nunes has recovered from an ankle injury and is fit to start, while Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki, Josko Gvardiol and Allan also come into the side following last weekend’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham.

Ruben Dias, Abdukodir Khusanov, Phil Foden, Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku all revert to the substitutes' bench for the visit of the Serie A side.

While Nunes will begin at right-back, Gvardiol is set to start at centre-back alongside Marc Guehi, with Nico O'Reilly retaining his spot at left-back.

Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi will continue to link arms in centre-midfield, with Fernandez expected to operate further forward in an advanced central role behind striker and captain Erling Haaland.

This could therefore see playmaker Rayan Cherki move out wide, with the Frenchman potentially occupying the left flank as Allan most likely begins on the right.

As for Napoli, head coach Massimiliano Allegri has made a total of three changes to the side that began the 1-0 win over Torino 04 in Serie A last weekend.

It has been revealed that kevin De Bruyne has been recalled to start against his former club for the second time since leaving in 2025. The legendary Belgian playmaker was sacrificed just 21 minutes into his first Etihad homecoming last season, following an early red card for captain Matteo Politano in a 2-0 defeat.

Defender Mathias Olivera and forward Noa Lang have also returned to Napoli’s first XI, with Rafa Marin, Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa and Antonio Vergara all making way.

Scotland duo Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay – who scored the match-winner against Torino – will both start in centre-midfield, while ex-Man United striker Rasmus Hojlund will be supported by Lang in attack.

Sunderland welcome Jagiellonia to the Stadium of Light on Thursday as they aim to build on positive results against Chelsea and Aston Villa either side of the international break.

The Black Cats have picked up more points in their last four Premier League games (five – W1 D2 L1) than they had in their first seven this season (four – W1 D1 L5).

But they have been missing captain Xhaka, who sustained a calf injury against Chelsea, while Brobbey has been suffering with a problem in his thigh over the last few weeks.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Le Bris ruled out Xhaka and Brobbey of their upcoming European match, while saying it was unlikely they would feature against Tottenham this weekend in the Premier League.

Le Bris' side travel to Anfield to face Liverpool next week before turning their attention to the Tyne-Wear derby against rivals Newcastle United on December 6.

"They are doing well, both are in a better place and are being assessed weekly," Le Bris told reporters.

"They want to play, but we need to take care of them because the season will be long. So they won't be available for this week, but we will see after [this week].".

With Dan Ballard also missing with a hamstring injury, Sunderland are missing the spine of their team.

"Jules [Ahoka] is a great example, coming from nowhere and able to play against Chelsea and Villa.".

Sunderland have already faced Polish opposition in the Europa League this season, drawing 1-1 with Lech Poznan. They are the first English club to face two Polish clubs in one major European season, and will want to bounce back from their defeat to Dinamo Zagreb last time out.

But their problems in the competition in 2026-27 have been in front of goal. Jagiellonia have, however, lost their last two Europa League matches, both without scoring. They have never lost three major European games in a row, nor have they failed to score in three in a row.

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a big future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

In a recent development, ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.
